text.t: Actin is a U-shaped protein, and many of them join together to build actin filaments.
This file holds a single rabbit actin, not a whole filament.
Deep in the groove between the two arms sits the nucleotide, here ADP.
Actin carries ATP when it joins a filament, then splits it to ADP, and ADP-actin lets go more easily.
Small calcium ions are bound around the protein, and one of them holds onto a phosphate of the ADP.
Filaments do not form neat crystals, so this actin was chemically modified to stop it joining filaments.
The file also holds a small dye molecule attached to the protein, called tetramethylrhodamine.
Compared with actin holding ATP, this ADP form shows a marked change of shape in one region, called subdomain 2.

does.t: Actin filaments form a scaffold inside cells, part of the cytoskeleton that gives a cell its shape.
They are also the track that myosin climbs to make muscles contract.
Actin can make up about 5 percent of the protein in a typical cell and up to one fifth in muscle cells.

shape.t: Each actin grips its nucleotide in a groove between two arms, and whether it holds ATP or ADP changes how tightly it binds in a filament.
Because new ATP-actin adds at one end while ADP-actin falls off the other, a filament can treadmill through the cell.
A microfilament is two intertwined strands of actin.

text.t: Actin fills the cytoplasm of animal, plant and fungal cells as a tangle of filaments.
Actin and myosin are plentiful in muscle cells.

wrong.t: Phalloidin, a poison from the death cap mushroom, makes actin filaments grow out of control.
The cells clog with rigid filaments, causing fatal liver and kidney damage.

history.who: L.R. Otterbein, P. Graceffa and R. Dominguez

text.t: Earlier actin structures were all caught bound to other proteins, such as DNase I, profilin or gelsolin.
This was actin on its own, in the ADP state, solved at 1.54 angstroms.

compare.t: One actin measures about 7.4 nm from end to end in this file.
A whole actin filament, or microfilament, is about 7 nm wide and the narrowest fibre of the cytoskeleton.

text.t: This calcium ion binds to the ADP.
